nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How do anthropogenic activities impact fish biodiversity globally?
nodes.answer: They severely affect fish biodiversity in more than half of the 2,456 river basins worldwide.
nodes.paragraph: Indeed, the fresh- water biodiversity loss in the Anthropocene is already pervasive in all taxonomic groups (Reid et al., 2019; Rivaes et al., 2021; Tickner et al., 2020), which experienced a more rapid decline (76%) compared to terrestrial and marine environments (39%) (McLellan et al., 2014). According to the most recent report by Su et al. (2021), anthropogenic activi- ties severely affect fish biodiversity in more than half of the 2,456 river basins worldwide. In Southeast Asia (SEA), freshwater environments play critical socioeconomic and cul- tural roles and host global hotspots of biodiversity and endemism, yet remain among the most threatened in the world (Coleman et al., 2019; Hughes, 2017; Sodhi et al., 2009). The freshwater biota in SEA also received less attention and investments compared to their terrestrial, marine, or temperate counterparts (Coleman et al., 2019; Tydecks et al., 2018), particularly in the Philippines (Magbanua et al., 2017; Papa & Briones, 2017; van der Ploeg et al., 2017).

nodes.question: What does the environmental pillar of the three-pillar model incorporate in terms of sustainability?
nodes.answer: The environmental pillar incorporates indicators related to the physical environment, such as greenhouse gas emissions and eutrophication of waterways.
nodes.paragraph: 2019). This framing of sustainability is sometimes referred to as triple- bottom line, or people, planet, profit (Purvis et al. 2019 ). The three-pillar model has also been described as economically dominant (James and Magee 2016) and anthropocentric (Purvis et al. 2019). This three-pillar approach may there- fore be an inappropriate conceptual framework for viewing agricultural sustainability as it has a foundation in business and therefore different ontological perspectives (Purvis et al. 2019). There is likely contention regarding definitions within these three pillars. However, for the purpose of this review, is can be broadly described where the environmental pil- lar incorporates indicators for the physical environment for example, indicators relating to greenhouse gas emissions or eutrophication of waterways; the social pillar incorporates community-based considerations for example, indicators relating to education and access to decent livelihood; the economic pillar incorporates classical fiscal indicators, for example, return on investment and profitability. A literature review conducted by Chopin et al. (2021) explored on-farm sustainability assessment tools and con- cluded a wider framing is required when undertaking agri- cultural sustainability measurements due to emergent rea- sons including resilience and stability.

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does the economic impact of water supply disruption from the Selangor River in Malaysia affect sustainability efforts in the region?
nodes.answer: The economic impact of water supply disruption from the Selangor River in Malaysia can have significant implications on sustainability efforts in the region, as it can disrupt various sectors dependent on water, such as agriculture, industry, and households, leading to economic losses and challenges in maintaining environmental sustainability.
